title: Comms Plan
description: The part-by-part build plan for ONE channel of ONE change. Channel-neutral and auditable: QA runs on this, and production (Stage 3b) is routed from it via channel_registry.json. The briefing_deck shape stays key-compatible with proposal_plan.json so cm-proposal-generator's build_deck.py validates it against a client .potx unchanged.

brief_ref.description: Path to the change_brief.json this plan draws on. The link that lets one brief serve many channel runs.

design_provenance.description: Who authored the DESIGN, as distinct from the copy. 'generated-unapproved' means a tool invented the layout (Canva generate-design, or a from-scratch deck) — the copy may have passed QA but the design still needs client sign-off before publish. Set by the producer, reported at handover.

channel.description: Exactly one per run. Cross-channel consistency comes from the shared brief, never from copying text between drafts. Each channel routes to a producer declared in channel_registry.json.

client.description: Carried onto the produced artifact — deck footers, document headers.

engagement_title.description: The change title. Becomes the document or deck title, so populate it alongside client for any produced artifact.

target_audience_ids.description: Which segments THIS run addresses. Coverage is computed against this subset, not the whole brief — a single-audience email must not fail for omitting messages aimed elsewhere.

template.description: The client's approved .potx for the briefing_deck channel. Omit it and the from-scratch route applies, which must be labelled UNAPPROVED TEMPLATE at handover.

slide_budget.description: Permitted but discouraged. Prefer brand_profile.channel_specs.briefing_deck.max_slides, which qa_comms.py enforces as a stated limit.

message_ids.description: The analogue of proposal_plan's requirement_ids. Nothing in the render path reads this field, so the rename is free.

slides.description: One output unit each — a slide for briefing_deck, a titled part for the other channels. The key is named 'slides' on purpose: renaming it would force a change to build_deck.py, and that compatibility is what buys the deck channel for free.

part_kind.description: Shapes the markdown output and drives the channel-spec checks in Stage 4.

layout.description: Required for briefing_deck only. Must name a layout present in the template profile.

speaker_notes.description: Every content slide in a cascade deck needs these. A deck without notes gets improvised, and the improvisation is what the audience remembers.

allOf.$comment: briefing_deck needs a title for the produced file. It does NOT require a template: omitting one selects the from-scratch route, which is legitimate and is labelled UNAPPROVED TEMPLATE at handover.

placeholder.description: Placeholder name from the template profile. Required for the briefing_deck channel; ignored by the markdown renderer.

kind.description: Same vocabulary as proposal_plan, so one plan renders to markdown and to every producer. 'table' carries a video shot list; 'phases' carries a milestone timeline.

sources.description: Provenance. Each entry is either a knowledge-bank entry ID or a 'brief:<dotted.path>' reference into change_brief.json. MUST be non-empty unless gap is true. See SKILL.md — this skill has THREE valid provenance states, not the proposal generator's two.

gap.description: True when neither the bank nor the brief covers it. Renders as a visible [GAP]; never substitute generated filler.

gap_note.description: Required when gap is true — what is missing and which message or action it leaves exposed.
